pages.quiz:
GEOGRAPHY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: GEOGRAPHY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Map Reading and Interpretation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Map Reading and Interpretation never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Map Reading and Interpretation as rumours only.
   C. Explain Map Reading and Interpretation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Map Reading and Interpretation.

2. Which statement about Folding is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Folding with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Say Folding never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Folding.
   D. Treat Folding as rumours only.

3. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Plan income and spending wisely
   B. Avoid saving forever
   C. Ignore prices in shops
   D. Hide all money underground

4. Which statement about Geographic Information Systems is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Geographic Information Systems never happens in Kenya.
   B. Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Geographic Information Systems.
   D. Treat Geographic Information Systems as rumours only.

5. Which statement about Vulcanicity is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Vulcanicity.
   B. Say Vulcanicity never happens in Kenya.
   C. Explain Vulcanicity with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Treat Vulcanicity as rumours only.

6. Which statement about Energy is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Energy never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Energy as rumours only.
   C. Explain Energy with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Energy.

7. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Explain symbols used on a map
   B. Measure rainfall only
   C. Name the president
   D. Replace the compass rose

8. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nakuru
   C. Mombasa
   D. Nairobi

9. Which statement about Agriculture is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Agriculture with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Agriculture as rumours only.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Agriculture.
   D. Say Agriculture never happens in Kenya.

10. Which statement about Industry is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Industry as rumours only.
   B. Explain Industry with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Say Industry never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Industry.

11. Which statement about Introduction to Geography is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Introduction to Geography never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Introduction to Geography.
   C. Explain Introduction to Geography with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Treat Introduction to Geography as rumours only.

12. Which statement about Earthquakes is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Earthquakes as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Earthquakes.
   C. Say Earthquakes never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Earthquakes with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Geography and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Map Reading and Interpretation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Statistical Methods and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Geographic Information Systems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
